title: Irreducibility of an affine linear incidence hypersurface
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is an integral domain. Let $r\geq1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$, with at least one $f_i\ne0$. Set $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Assume every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ minimal among those containing $J$ has height at least two. Here height is the supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals ending at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; when $J=A$ the condition is vacuous. Then the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(\sum_{i=1}^r f_ix_i))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Reducedness of this quotient is not asserted.

proof.text: Put $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $L=\sum_i f_ix_i$. Reindex so that $f_1\ne0$. The coefficient of $x_1$ shows $L\ne0$. Adjoining $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ to a finite set of algebra generators of $A$ exhibits $B$ as a finite type $k$-algebra. Thus $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], and it is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain].

By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], $D_j$ is a domain and its coefficient map $A_j	o D_j$ is injective. Evaluation $\psi_j:B	o D_j$, fixing $A$ and $x_i$ for $i

e0$ and a product mapping to zero in a domain has a factor mapping to zero. Moreover $L\in K_j$ and $K_j\cap A=(0)$.

proof.text: For $h\in K_j$, regard $h$ as a polynomial in $x_j$ over $D_j$. Substitution at $c_j$ gives $h(c_j)=0$, so $h=(x_j-c_j)g=f_j^{-1}Lg$ for some polynomial $g$ over $D_j$. This divisibility is an explicit calculation: apply $y^m-c^m=(y-c)\sum_{t=0}^{m-1}y^{m-1-t}c^t$ to each positive-degree monomial of $h$, and subtract $h(c_j)$. There are only finitely many coefficients of $f_j^{-1}g$, each with a power of $f_j$ as denominator. Multiplying by one sufficiently large power $f_j^N$ puts them all in $A[x_i:i\ne j]$, giving $f_j^Nh=Lv$ with $v\in B$. The identity holds in $B$ because its map into $A_j[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is injective coefficient by coefficient. Consequently every $h\in K_j$ has $f_j^Nh\in(L)$ for some $N\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, affine incidence paragraph, lines 9089–9132; algebraic expansion of the elimination and codimension argument

proof.text: Let $Q$ be any prime of $B$ minimal over $(L)$. Its image $\overline Q=Q/(L)$ in $B/(L)$ is a minimal prime: a smaller prime would have a smaller prime inverse image containing $(L)$, contradicting minimality of $Q$. Conversely primes below $\overline Q$ lift to primes below $Q$ by taking inverse images, and passing back to the quotient recovers each ideal. Thus there is no strict chain of primes below $\overline Q$, so $\operatorname{ht}(\overline Q)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $R=B$, $t=1$, $f_1=L$, $J=(L)$, $\mathfrak P=Q$. Noetherianity was proved in step 1, and $(L)\subseteq Q$. It gives $\operatorname{ht}(Q)\leq\operatorname{ht}(\overline Q)+1=1$.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, affine incidence paragraph, lines 9089–9132; algebraic expansion of the elimination and codimension argument

proof.text: Suppose every $f_i$ belongs to $Q$. Its contraction $p=Q\cap A$ is prime and contains $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] there is a prime $p_0\subseteq p$ minimal over $J$. The hypothesis gives $\operatorname{ht}(p_0)\geq2$, hence there are primes $p_a\subsetneq p_b\subsetneq p_0$ (truncate a chain ending at $p_0$ if necessary). For any prime $u$ of $A$, the coefficient reduction map $B\to(A/u)[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ has kernel $uB$: a polynomial maps to zero exactly when all its coefficients lie in $u$, which is exactly membership in the ideal generated by $u$. Its target is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]; thus $uB$ is prime and $uB\cap A=u$. We obtain $p_aB\subsetneq p_bB\subsetneq p_0B\subseteq Q$, where strictness follows by contracting coefficients. This is a chain of length at least two ending at $Q$ (append $Q$ if the last inclusion is strict), contrary to step 4. Therefore some $f_j\notin Q$; this argument also covers $J=A$, since then no prime $p$ could contain $J$.

proof.text:
Choose $j$ with $f_j
otin Q$. This coefficient is nonzero, so steps 2–3 apply. If $h\in K_j$, then $f_j^Nh\in(L)\subseteq Q$; primality and $f_j
otin Q$ imply $h\in Q$. Hence $(L)\subseteq K_j\subseteq Q$. Since $K_j$ is prime and $Q$ is minimal over $(L)$, $Q=K_j$. In particular $Q\cap A=(0)$, so $f_1
otin Q$. Applying the same argument at $j=1$ gives $Q=K_1$. At least one such minimal prime exists: $K_1$ is a proper prime containing $(L)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] supplies a prime minimal over $(L)$ inside $K_1$. Thus $K_1$ is the unique prime minimal over $(L)$.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, affine incidence paragraph, lines 9089–9132; algebraic expansion of the elimination and codimension argument

proof.text: Put $R=B/(L)$ and $\overline K=K_1/(L)$. This is a prime ideal: $R/\overline K=B/K_1$ injects into the domain $D_1$. Every prime $P$ of $R$ has prime inverse image $\widetilde P$ in $B$ containing $(L)$; [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] puts a prime minimal over $(L)$ inside $\widetilde P$. Step 6 identifies it with $K_1$, so $\overline K\subseteq P$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R=V(\overline K)$. This set is nonempty (it contains $\overline K$) and irreducible by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. This proves exactly the asserted irreducibility, without claiming $R$ is reduced.
